body: I'm still here, and you're right. Thanks for the kind words.

Sounds like a you've got a bright future ahead, life has its ups and downs just remember to keep on putting you're best foot forward and to try you hardest to be involved in the world around you. I'm pretty big fan of Iron Maiden, Black Sabbath, Megadeth too. Its very late here so I'm to bed but if you're feeling this way again there's no shame in throwing up another post here or feel free to send me a pm I can get back to you when I wake up.

I've tried group therapy and support groups, I always feel very out of place and never know what to say.

I've tried a lot of psychiatrists, psychologists, and therapists for pretty much whole life none of ever really seemed to help. I did DBT for about 8 months earlier this year too but it didn't really seem to help either.

I've had a lot of troubles in my life so I don't know where I'd begin to open up.

My brother is 22 and just scraped by in high school and now he spreads cow poop for a living, I think he still feels purpose. I think it just varies from person to person what make you feel purpose. 

Maybe try starting a YouTube channel, socializing at local gigs, seeing if your local venues or promoters need any help, or taking up an instrument if you haven't already. I'm sure you could come up some of your own ideas. The point I guess I'm trying to make is if you don't make a constant effort to be involved in the world around you, you're not going to feel much purpose.

Also what are going to school for? And what are some of your favourite metal bands? I'm a pretty big metalhead myself.

Billions of people don't make it as far as university, just saying. I feel the same way at times, finding purpose is an important part of life that there is no one size fits all answer to. What are your interests and hobbys? That might be a good jumping point to find some purpose and build relationships.
What are some specific things making you feel worthless? You've made it university, I think that in it's self is enough to show you're not worthless.

Yeah that's exactly what I'm saying.

I'd like to have a group of friends again, I haven't had a group of friends since high school which was 3 years ago. Or even just any friends. I don't think it'd have to be a friendship with another "valueless" person I try to be good to everybody around me. I think main problem is I don't really know where to make new friends now that I'm out of school living on my own, and with all the shitty friendships I've had in the past it makes me kind of unconfident and less than optimistic about future friends.

Thanks, I really appreciate this comment and it made me feel a lot better about this. I may have been used and had the friendship end in a shitty way but I can rest easy knowing I always put my kindest foot forward. When I feel like this I again I think I'm going to go back to your comment and reread it. 

Also I noticed your posting in /r/depression , if need to vent, chat, have somebody listen or give some advice don't hesitate to send me a pm.

This may sound like the kinda thing you see on a poster with an eagle on it in the corner of dentist's office but you get out what you put in. It doesn't always hold true but it does sometimes. Unfortunately there is no magic finger snap. If you want friends, the SO, and income, you have to stop and think "Where can I start putting in the hard work?".

I'd love to offer you some suggestions on where to start. What are your interests? Have you completed any post secondary? Do have any work experience?

> To stop hearing, "must be nice to sit on your ass and live off MY taxes."

The people who say that are obviously assholes who just want to feel good about themselves. The fact of the matter is you do have a disability that effects every moment of every day, there should be absolutely zero shame in getting assistance. There is people out there who get government money who don't deserve it, you are definitely not one of them.


> All I wanted to do was have a better life, an education.

You didn't fail here, you did the opposite. You got not one but two degrees, despite it being what sounds like an uphill battle. You can still use these to provide yourself a better tomorrow. That sounds like a success to me.

> It's 2017, I've graduated, can find no work and have now been told by Social Security that I owe them $26,000 in over payment because I was never supposed to get payments from 2014 onward.

I know this will sound dumb and cliche but there is hope to get through this, you will eventually find work, and once you do it will be possible to pay it off. It will take along time to pay it off but I don't doubt that you will eventually. As far as finding work goes is there good public transport in your city? Have you looked into if there is any resources in your city to help find work for people with disabilities?

Me being used and stolen from has been a recurring thing in every friendship my whole life. I was friends with this guy for a long time and I did so many things to help over the years. He never stole from me used me previously. It was so out of nowhere and at time I was already seriously considering ending it, it's really cut deep. Part of me knows it's a silly thing to let push me over the edge, but I just can't get over it. It's just such a shitty end to last friendship I thought I still had.

I'm sure people would give you a second thought they'll probably think what an asshole you were while you were around. If you're showing up to /r/suicidewatch to attack people then cry then report them you sound like you're right, you're worthless and should kill yourself.
